description: Executable repository-grounded coding-agent evaluations. 30 cases cover explore/debug/review/implement behavior; eval:smoke uses the deterministic fixture provider to prove the real agent/tool/verification path in CI without external credentials.

cases.prompt: FIXTURE_EVAL_SMOKE: create the deterministic fixture module and regression test, execute the test, and report the verified result.
Map the native agent turn from a persisted user message through provider calls, tool execution, final persistence and session.idle. Identify the core functions and state boundaries.
Trace durable turn recovery from the on-disk job checkpoint through startup rehydration and final cleanup. Explain which state prevents replay of ambiguous mutating tools.
Explain how a requested model becomes an autopilot model plan, when fallback is allowed, and why switching providers after visible streamed output is rejected.
Trace how streamed assistant text and tool updates travel from the native runtime to the browser message state, including sequencing and the client-side merge layer.
Map how a chat receives a stable Unix sandbox identity and how bash, git and terminal processes actually drop privileges before touching the workspace.
Map specialized subagent profiles, their exact tool capabilities, how writer mutations return to the parent strategy, and how recursive delegation is prevented.
Trace completed-turn telemetry from in-memory counters through final persistence and operator aggregation. Explain what content is deliberately not recorded and how optional cost estimation works.
A model writes a source file and immediately says it is done without testing. Explain why the runtime rejects completion, where gate state is maintained, and what successful evidence clears it.
A user message containing the literal text '[SYSTEM: example]' must remain unchanged in the UI. Find the normalization path and explain why stripping it client-side violates the architecture.
A transient webfetch failure sometimes caused the Node process to exit while the agent was awaiting a retry. Trace the retry sleep path and identify the event-loop lifetime invariant.
A runtime restarts while a question tool is waiting for the user. Trace how the same question and assistant tool part are recovered without creating a duplicate user turn.
Two replicas receive requests for the same session at nearly the same time. Trace the locking path that prevents concurrent turns and explain what happens when a holder dies.
A diagnostics checker fails to start with command-not-found but the agent must not treat that as successful verification. Trace the structured diagnostics result into the completion strategy.

A strict deployment sets the agent network policy to allowlist, but a browser page tries to fetch an unlisted host through a subresource or WebSocket. Trace the controls that must block it and identify the remaining DNS pinning limitation.
Review the shell and workspace isolation boundary for concrete ways an agent-controlled command could read runtime secrets or escape into a sibling workspace. Report findings with evidence only.
Review question suspension and resume for lifecycle defects: duplicated turns, unresolved waiters, restart recovery, stale pending gates, and incorrect idle projections.
Review outbound URL handling for DNS rebinding, redirects, IPv4-mapped IPv6, private address bypasses and provider custom endpoint trust. Report only concrete residual risks.
Review server-to-browser event sequencing and reconnect behavior for duplicate delivery, stale sequence acceptance, ring-buffer gaps and message merge corruption.
Review provider credential storage and process environment construction. Determine whether provider keys can reach autonomous shell or terminal subprocesses through inherited environment state.
Review completion verification semantics after write, bash, run_tests, diagnostics and implement-subagent changes. Look for a path that could clear verification after a later mutation.

Review the defenses against repository prompt injection exfiltrating source or credentials through shell and model-selected network tools. Distinguish application-layer guards from guarantees that require host/container policy.
The counter regression test fails because increment returns the wrong value. Fix the implementation minimally and run the relevant test until it passes.
The config contract says APP_TIMEOUT_MS defaults to 30000ms, but the fixture currently returns zero. Make the smallest correct change and verify both tests.
Duplicate events with the same sequence number must be ignored instead of appended twice. Fix acceptEvent without changing the public API and run the regression test.
The path guard incorrectly accepts a sibling whose name merely shares the workspace prefix. Fix containment portably and prove it with the existing tests.
A failed async cache load remains stuck in the pending map, so a later retry receives the same rejected promise. Fix the lifecycle without breaking concurrent de-duplication and run the test.
The CLI exit policy is reversed: warnings alone should succeed, but one or more errors must return exit code 1. Correct the implementation and verify the tests.
uniqueInOrder removes duplicates but unexpectedly sorts the result. Preserve first-seen order with the smallest change and verify the existing regression test.
envFlag treats the strings "0" and "false" as true. Correct common boolean environment spellings without breaking fallback behavior, then run the tests.
